pairs.subject: runner-fleet
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/cron/rescan/route.ts:3 These routes run scan work as an application-level durable ScanJob queue, drained inside a Vercel serverless invocation with a fixed SCAN_CONCURRENCY. They do not provision, type, scale or isolate CI runners. The golden path hands application concurrency and job coordination to concurrency-guards and job-coordination. A search of the context's directories for runs-on, actions-runner, autoscal and hashFiles found nothing. The words 'queue', 'fleet' and 'runner' do appear, but they name the scan queue, the repo fleet and the standing-runner drive rows.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/cron/rescan/route.ts:120 The queue depth read here belongs to the app's ScanJob table and is reported as a remainder. It does not drive the size of any runner fleet, so the technique's precondition (elastic runner capacity) does not hold.

src/app/api/org/import/route.ts:503 This is a per-repo lease claim at the application level, which is concurrency-guards/job-coordination territory. It is not a delivery-system exclusion over deploys or migrations.
src/app/api/org/import/route.ts:516 One in-process drain with a fixed concurrency. It has no runner types and no capability matching.

pairs.subject: runner-fleet
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/segments.ts:2 This context is CRUD for org-scoped repo segment tags: db functions, API routes, a client hook and a selector. It executes no delivery work and has no runners, pools, build caches or deploy lanes. A search of its directories for runs-on, actions-runner, autoscal and hashFiles found nothing. The 'fleet' in segments.ts means the org's set of repositories, and 'concurrent' means concurrent UI edits.

techniques.evidence: src/features/standing/repositories/useRepoSegmentsPanel.ts:124 The only concurrency here is a client-state update between UI edits, not a serialized delivery lane.
